title: U.S. Senate · Kansas

context.text: Incumbent Roger Marshall (R) defeated Pond Naramore in the August 4, 2026 Republican primary, 79.8% to 20.2%. Adam Hamilton won the Democratic primary in an 11-candidate field with 34.9% of the vote. David Graham advanced as the Libertarian Party's candidate.

summary.text: Roger Marshall is the Republican incumbent U.S. Senator from Kansas, first elected in 2020 after one term in the U.S. House representing Kansas's 1st District. A physician and former obstetrician-gynecologist from Great Bend, he is a U.S. Army Reserve veteran. According to his Senate website, he serves on the Agriculture, Finance, Health, Education, Labor and Pensions, and Budget committees.

background.text: Born in El Dorado, Kansas, in 1960, and raised in Butler County; according to his Senate website, he is a fifth-generation farm kid and the first in his family to attend college.
Earned an associate degree from Butler Community College (1980), a B.S. in biochemistry from Kansas State University, and an M.D. from the University of Kansas School of Medicine (1987).
Served in the U.S. Army Reserve from 1984 to 1991, reaching the rank of captain.
Practiced as an OB/GYN in Great Bend for more than 25 years. According to his Senate website, he delivered more than 5,000 babies and owned a practice that grew from 5 to more than 300 employees.
In 1998 he and eight other doctors opened Great Bend Regional Medical Center. He owned Heartland Regional OBGYN from 1998 to 2012 and was co-owner from 2013 to 2019.
Served as a Rotary International district governor and, according to his Senate website, as an elder, deacon and board chairman of his church.

Defeated incumbent Rep. Tim Huelskamp in the August 2016 Republican primary, 56% to 44%, and won the general election with 65.9%. He represented Kansas's 1st District from January 2017 to January 2021, serving on the House Agriculture Committee.

Won the 2020 Republican Senate primary with 40.3% of the vote in a field including Kris Kobach, then defeated Democratic state Sen. Barbara Bollier 53% to 42% in the general election. He took office on January 3, 2021.
In the Senate he chairs the Agriculture subcommittee on Conservation, Forestry, Natural Resources, and Biotechnology and the HELP subcommittee on Primary Health and Retirement Security.
According to his Senate website, he and his wife, Laina, have four children and five grandchildren.

positions.summary: In a February 2025 statement, Marshall backed President Trump's imposition of reciprocal tariffs.
positions.quote: Reciprocal tariffs are strong, strategic negotiating tools that ultimately strike better trade deals, ensure long-term economic growth and strengthen our national security.

positions.summary: Marshall joined Senate Republicans in introducing a resolution calling on the NCAA to revoke its transgender student-athlete eligibility policy and to protect girls' and women's sports.
In a June 2026 interview, Marshall said the Senate needs to pass the SAVE America Act, discussing its voter ID and proof-of-citizenship provisions.
positions.quote: if we want to save this republic, then we need to pass the SAVE America Act.

record.text: Serves on the Senate Committee on Health, Education, Labor, and Pensions.

candidates.name: Adam Hamilton
candidates.ballotNote: Won the August 4 Democratic primary in an 11-candidate field

summary.text: Adam Hamilton is the Democratic nominee for U.S. Senate in Kansas. A United Methodist pastor and author, he founded the Church of the Resurrection in the Kansas City area in 1990, which is now the largest United Methodist congregation in the country. He won the August 4, 2026 Democratic primary with 34.9% of the vote and campaigns on affordability, health care and ending corruption in Washington.

background.text: Born July 12, 1964, and raised in Prairie Village, Kansas. Describes himself as a fifth-generation Kansan whose ancestors settled in Dickinson County.
Graduated from Blue Valley High School in 1982 and earned a B.A. in pastoral ministry from Oral Roberts University in 1985.
Earned a Master of Divinity from the Perkins School of Theology at Southern Methodist University.

Founded the United Methodist Church of the Resurrection in the Kansas City area in 1990 with his wife, LaVon, and remains its senior pastor; he says it began with four people and is now the largest United Methodist church in the country.
Has written more than 30 books about Christian faith and contemporary issues, according to Wikipedia.
Says the church is the largest source of donated food in Kansas City after the regional food bank and runs a mobile dental clinic and school-support programs.
Won the Democratic nomination in the August 4, 2026 primary, defeating ten other candidates including Christy Davis and Noah Taylor. KCUR reports he lives in Stillwell, Kansas.

priorities.text: Affordability: wants to end tariffs, crack down on price-gouging, expand housing construction, and pursue trade and tax policy he says would help Kansas families, farmers and small businesses.
Health care: wants to reverse Medicaid cuts he says threaten rural hospitals, restore expired ACA premium tax credits, and let Medicare negotiate more drug prices.

Government reform: supports term limits and age limits for federal officeholders, a ban on members of Congress trading individual stocks, halting congressional pay during shutdowns, and says his campaign takes no corporate PAC money.

positions.summary: Hamilton's issues page calls for reversing Medicaid cuts, restoring the ACA subsidies, and expanding Medicare drug price negotiation.
positions.quote: Reverse the cuts to Medicaid and restore the ACA subsidies that hold premiums down.

positions.summary: Hamilton's issues page calls for ending tariffs and requiring congressional approval for new tariffs.
positions.quote: End self-destructive tariffs and unnecessary wars

candidates.researchNotes: Reviewed his campaign issues page (hamiltonforkansas.com/issues) in full and his Ballotpedia survey responses. His housing plan does not mention zoning, so housing_supply is a statement only. Endorsements listed on that survey: Tim Kaine, Kathleen Sebelius.

statements.quote: Congress should make it easier to buy a home and easier to build one.
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page

statements.quote: Protect a woman’s right to choose and prevent further government interference into personal decisions
statements.context: On his campaign website's issues page, in a sentence that also proposes codifying access to contraception

candidates.name: David Graham
candidates.ballotNote: Advanced as the Libertarian Party of Kansas nominee
candidates.currentRole: Libertarian Party of Kansas Vice Chair

summary.text: David Graham is the Libertarian Party of Kansas Vice Chair and the party's 2026 U.S. Senate nominee. He previously ran for the same seat in 2022, receiving about 3.0% of the general-election vote. Little biographical information about him is publicly available.

background.text: Is from Overland Park, Kansas, according to KCUR.
In 2022, his campaign website described him as a lawyer and said he would work to reduce the size of government, reform criminal justice and take a more defensive approach to national defense.
Was the Libertarian nominee for U.S. Senate in Kansas in 2022, receiving 29,766 votes (about 3.0%) in a race won by Jerry Moran.

Serves as Libertarian Party of Kansas Vice Chair and is the party's 2026 U.S. Senate candidate. KCUR reported he did not appear to have an active campaign website or social media accounts and did not respond to a request for campaign materials.

candidates.researchNotes: Graham has not completed Ballotpedia's Candidate Connection survey for 2026 or 2022, and no campaign website was found. Public record is limited to Ballotpedia election data. Searches in October 2026 found no campaign website or social accounts; an Axios voter guide excerpt appeared in search results but the page could not be loaded, so nothing from it is used.
